title: Do consumers vote with their feet in response to negative ESG news? Evidence from consumer foot traffic to retail locations

scopes.description: Complete supplied SAS and Stata workflow: main event-panel construction, spending and stacked branches, graph extensions, CAR and Google branches, ESG/traffic and sales aggregation, industry distribution, Compustat comparison, and GSS survey analysis. The producer-first sequence and cross-language output handoffs are reviewed with explicit unresolved gaps. The CAR branch uses DSI, DSENAMES, DSF and DSEDELIST as separate required raw components; partial local matches do not satisfy the joint workflow.

issues.description: Separate one-row probes establish readable PM news fields and separate company-identifier fields, but they do not verify one matching product/field contract for the composite author input. Exact News Legacy equivalence, the RepRisk_ID-to-ISIN join and the author's primary_ISIN versus all_ISINs choice, and 2018–2020 history remain unresolved.

The main sample begins after 10 Jan 2018 and the graph preparation builds a −21 to −11 pre-event window, so the earliest included events can require December 2017 traffic. The supplied filter only removes years after 2020; no local history probe verifies the required 2017 tail.

The readable SAS graph block constructs pre-event observations, while the Stata extensions append graph_ext_day.dta and include +30, +45, +48 and +60 analyses. The remaining SAS producer/export block is unread, so its exact file path, schema and positive post-event coverage cannot be verified; this does not establish that those rows are absent.

SAS constructs the main, spending and stacked event panels, and Stata consumes files with the corresponding names, but the SAS export destinations are masked. Confirm the actual output paths, formats and run order before invoking the consumers.

The CAR SAS program exports its generated ticnews table to a masked path, while the Stata dependency inventory expects rep_car.dta; the intended file alias, export format, fields and producer-to-consumer path are not verified.

The readable SAS source creates and consumes allcar as the merged CAR aggregate, while the frozen dependency inventory identifies a work.car intermediate. The supplied source does not prove these are the same artifact or session object.
The Google SAS program exports googleesg to a masked path, while the Stata dependency inventory expects google.dta. The intended alias, format, path and required columns remain unverified.

The ESG/traffic SAS program exports sg3 and rep5 to masked paths, while Stata expects month_esg_ft.dta and esg_qtr_sale.dta. The intended file aliases, formats, paths and variable contracts remain unverified.
SAS9 exports qcompustat to a masked path, while the Stata comparison dependency expects comp_compare.dta. Confirm the actual alias, output format, location and field contract.

The CAR, Google and industry programs import prepared ticker/news-date or ticker/industry mapping files, but their quoted paths are masked and no supplied producer specifies the fields, identifiers, date vintage or coverage.

The dependency checklist includes a SAS WORK CRSP component, but the readable source windows do not establish its producer/session identity or its relation to the local CRSP tables. The remote connection block is masked; no SAS startup or configuration inspection resolves this.

The CAR macro visibly creates _evtrets_temp, but the source-join statement that defines its upstream table and session context is masked. Preserve it as a generated workflow intermediate while leaving that specific raw/producer link unresolved.

The bounded DSENAMES probe observed PERMNO, TICKER and name-date fields; its sampled field list did not include NCUSIP, while the visible CAR link branch selects NCUSIP. A compatible local product/field mapping has not been established; this probe does not establish product-wide absence.

The local CCMXPF_LNKHIST product has readable matching link fields, but the author source names crsp.ccmxpf_lnkhist2023. Its 2023 alias and event-date coverage are not verified by the unversioned local candidate.

The supplied code directly reads esgpref2018.dta, demo2018.dta, house2018.dta and naics_service.dta, and SAS reads crsp.ccmxpf_lnkhist2023; these direct input contracts are not represented by the frozen 62 dependency IDs. They are recorded as requirements without inventing checklist IDs.

The county crosswalk files are required by visible Stata merges, but their prepared variable definitions, FIPS representation, transformations, release/vintage and local file paths are not supplied. Public pages identify candidate products only and do not establish these prepared-file contracts.

NORC documents the 2021 individual-year Stata data, but the exact variable names, labels and missing-value handling required by the supplied Stata survey source are not confirmed against the downloaded file.

evidence.description: The datasheet identifies SafeGraph traffic, RepRisk news, Compustat quarterly fundamentals, ACS and House election data, and the firm-county-day merge level.
evidence.quote:
We aggregated the daily firm-store level data to the daily firm-county level.

We also downloaded the RepRisk News Legacy data from WRDS on September 16th, 2021.
and obtained firm quarterly financial characteristics from Compustat North America
Fundamentals Quarterly (downloaded on October 19th 2021). We first merged the SafeGraph
data with Compustat using company tickers, and then merged the resulting dataset with
RepRisk (via WRDS) using CUSIP. The final dataset contains observations at the firm-county-
day level. All RepRisk variables were obtained via WRDS, to which Fordham University has
institutional access.

We obtained county-level demographic variables from the 2018 American Community Survey
(US Census Bureau), downloaded on April 7th, 2021. We also obtained 2018 county-level U.S.
House of Representatives election results from the MIT Election Data and Science Lab
(MEDSL), downloaded on April 16th, 2023. We merge these datasets with the firm-county-day
level foot traffic data using FIPS (Federal Information Processing Standard) county codes.

This checkpoint records the source-chain and raw-input contract findings. Bounded catalog field probes, software command checks, public-source compatibility, the 62-edge dependency review and specific producer/consumer handoffs remain under review.
Route status separates verified local field/readability candidates from unresolved product equivalence, identifier, period and construction gaps. One-row probes establish columns/readability only.
The 2018 ACS, MEDSL, LCV, Yale, AFL-CIO and GSS sources are tied to the prepared-file contracts without inferring county aggregation or field compatibility from a public page.

Producer-first order reviewed: SAS1 main panel → main/alternative Stata; SAS2 spend → Stata3; SAS3 stacked → Stata4; SAS4 graph preparation → extension consumers; SAS5 CAR and SAS6 Google preparation → Stata6/7; SAS7 monthly/quarterly ESG products → Stata8; SAS9 Compustat comparison → Stata9; Stata10 survey is a separate GSS branch. SAS8 emits its own industry-distribution workbooks.

The CAR path imports a prepared ticker/news-date map, joins date-valid CCM history, uploads the linked rows to rep2, runs the event-study calls, downloads car1/car2/car3 into local WORK and aggregates/exports the result. Masked source statements leave specific WORK object and file alias handoffs unresolved.

All 62 frozen dependency IDs are reviewed once. Generated workflow products have empty target_ids; raw inputs retain their corresponding requirement links; unresolved session/alias/field edges remain explicit issues.

Visible Stata branches require +30, +45, +48 or +60 event windows; the readable SAS4 block establishes a −21 to −11 pre-window, while the remaining producer/export source is unread. This is an unresolved product/window contract, not a finding that rows or access are absent.
